title: Pinning legacy retirement and customer migration playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for retiring the legacy region-pinning mechanism (legacyPinToken) and migrating customers to the new territory-binding flow (pin-v2 / tenancy-anchor). The doc focuses on operational steps, customer impact analysis, telemetry, and rollback criteria. This is intentionally pragmatic — expect follow-ups (tickets linked above).

Summary of motivation:
- LegacyPinToken has incompatibilities with private deployments (edge anchors + VPC routing) and blocks multi-region failover logic.
- Pin-v2 adds audit metadata, stronger geo-constraints, and a clear entitlement field that the router and policy engine can consume.
- We must retire legacyPinToken to simplify routing code, reduce special-case fallbacks, and remove a source of inconsistent residency evidence.

High-level migration strategy:
1) Launch pin-v2 as opt-in for new tenants (already done: API stable).
2) Run a 90-day co-existence window where both tokens are honored but legacyPinToken is logged with higher severity to telemetry (flag: legacy_pin_warning=true).
3) Begin targeted opt-in nudges for tenants (month 0-2).
4) Start graduated enforcement: for low-risk tenants (internal, dev/qa) disable legacy acceptance after 90d; for high-risk/enterprise customers, negotiate migration SLAs and extended windows.
5) Full enforcement (reject legacy tokens) after customer migration: target 9 months from kickoff but adjustable based on customer commitments.

Stakeholders and RACI (short):
- Eng (API + routing): Responsible for rollout gates, feature flags, and telemetry events. (Owner: Liam Chen)
- SRE: Responsible for observability, capacity impact checks, and canarying. (Owner: Priya Nair)
- Solutions/CS: Customer outreach, migration assistance, and contract exceptions. (Owner: Diego Martinez)
- Product Legal: Approve any contract change or SLA modifications.
- Support: Runbooks and escalation paths.

Telemetry & success metrics (must be instrumented before enforcement):
- % of calls using legacyPinToken (by tenant, region, and account tier) — baseline and weekly trend.
- Error rate uplift when we disable legacy acceptance in a canary pool.
- Number of migration support tickets opened per week and mean time to close.
- Number of tenants with automated migration using the SDK script.
- False positive enforcement rate (calls rejected incorrectly) < 0.1% for production enforcement.

Operator checklist (pre-canary):
- [ ] Add legacy_pin_seen and legacy_pin_blocked telemetry events (schema versioned).
- [ ] Create dashboard with tenant breakout and top 50 tenants by legacy usage.
- [ ] Add feature flag: routing.accept_legacy_pin (global + per-tenant override).
- [ ] Smoke test: ensure pin-v2 tokens accepted across hosted/dedicated/private flows.
- [ ] Prepare emergency rollback: ability to re-enable legacy acceptance globally in <15m.

Canary plan (staged):
Stage A (internal):
- Target: internal accounts + sandbox tenants (~5% of traffic).
- Action: turn off legacy acceptance for this cohort; monitor for 72 hours.
- Rollback criteria: >0.5% production-wide latency increase or >0.2% increase in 5xxs attributable to pin errors.

Stage B (low-risk customers):
- Target: small non-SLA customers that opted-in to early migration.
- Action: disable legacy acceptance; support on slack + dedicated migration runbook.
- Monitor ticket volume and per-tenant error spikes for 7 days.

Stage C (enterprise customers):
- Target: tenants with contracts and region-SLA dependencies.
- Action: coordinate Migrations AB with Solutions Eng and legal; apply per-tenant feature flags when ready.

Customer communication (templates & cadence):
- Phase 0 (announcement): "We're introducing a safer, auditable region pin that enables better failover and compliance. Legacy pins will be retired — here's the timeline and migration options." (send 60 days before first enforcement)
- Phase 1 (reminder + migration offer): 30 days before: include migration SDK, one-click console migration, and invite to migration office hours.
- Phase 2 (pre-enforcement warning): 7 days before disabling legacy for their cohort, send explicit warning and migration links.
- Emergency/Exception request: CS can request a 30-day extension via ENG-1503 ticket and must provide migration plan.

Migration tools & automation:
- SDK helper: pin-migrate (python + node) that exchanges legacyPinToken for pin-v2, preserves audit fields, and reloads tenant bindings. (PR linked above — needs docs and tests).
- Console migration flow: quick toggle that issues pin-v2 from existing session when admin verifies region preference.
- Bulk CSV import: for customers with many sub-tenants. Support script checks for collisions and creates migration-change audit events.

Risk matrix (high-level):
- Risk: silent failures for embedded clients using very old SDKs. Mitigation: add user-agent telemetry, target those tenants in migration outreach, and provide embedded SDK patches.
- Risk: customer perceived data-movement when we re-anchor region metadata. Mitigation: include clear language that pin-v2 does not move stored data, only routing metadata.
- Risk: legal/regulatory objections for some sovereign customers. Mitigation: escalate to Product-Legal and offer extended timelines or on-prem migration assistance.

Rollback & emergency runbook:
- If enforcement causes >1% global error surge attributable to pin failures: enable routing.accept_legacy_pin globally and notify SRE oncall.
- If single large tenant (top 5) is impacted: re-enable per-tenant flag and open a dedicated migration incident with CS and Eng.

Open questions and TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Q: Do we want legacyPinToken to continue emitting residency evidence in audit logs post-retirement? Pros: historical trace. Cons: keeps old codepaths in critical flows. (Action: product to decide by 2025-01-20)
- Q: Billing/contract impact if region pin change triggers different pricing (rare). Need legal guidance.
- TODO: add templates for in-console banners and migration office hours sign-up page.
- TODO: schedule cross-functional cutover rehearsal with SRE and Solutions Eng (target week of 2025-02-05).

Customer migration priority heuristics (suggested):
1) Tenants with >50% legacy usage and no dedicated private deployment — high priority (easy fix).
2) Tenants on Private with bespoke routing (requires Solutions Eng) — high touch.
3) Tenants in regulated regions with contractual residency clauses — coordinate legal and offer extended timelines.

Estimated effort (rough):
- Eng infra work + telemetry: 3.5 engineer-months (split across routing, API, feature flags).
- SDK console + docs: 1.0 engineer-month.
- CS enablement + migrations: 0.8 PM-month + 1.0 SE-month over runway.

Appendix: sample escalation snippet for Support engineers:
- If a customer reports a sudden 403/422 during migration window: check tenant feature flags -> check legacy_pin_seen events -> escalate to Eng oncall with correlation_id and sample request headers.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc purposely mixes tactical runbook items with product/contract considerations — please flag anything that should be split into separate artifacts.
- Looking for approval/comments on: enforcement timeline (9 months default), rollback thresholds, and the customer communication cadence.

End of playbook (working draft).
